findings.summary: outcomes.yaml read-modify-write in _append_value has no lock; concurrent writers lose rows
findings.suggestion: Serialize _append_value's read-append-write with the repo's flock helper (worktree.py) on a sibling lock file.

reasoning.observe: Same RMW body existed in record_value at HEAD; the diff extracts it and adds measure_outcome/measure_all as new callers.
reasoning.trace: wrapup 5.7 offers measure --all at every wrapup and concurrent worktrees share the base; a manual record can race a measure run.
reasoning.infer: Both read N rows, both append, the later writer overwrites the earlier row silently.
reasoning.conclude: Pre-existing defect whose exposure this diff widens; a lock is proportionate.

findings.summary: TimeoutExpired kills only the direct child; grandchildren of measure.cmd outlive the declared timeout
findings.suggestion: Popen(argv, start_new_session=True) + communicate(timeout); on TimeoutExpired os.killpg(pid, SIGKILL) then wait, then raise WorldError('timeout').
findings.evidence: subprocess.run(argv, cwd=…, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=measure.timeout_s, check=False)

reasoning.observe: run()'s timeout path calls process.kill() on the child only; no process group is created.
reasoning.trace: measure.cmd is operator argv that commonly forks (uv run, pytest workers).
reasoning.infer: A forked grandchild keeps running past timeout_s holding ports/locks.
reasoning.conclude: The declared timeout is not an upper bound on the command's resource lifetime; process-group launch + group kill fixes it.

findings.summary: Select-failure WorldError messages embed raw stdout fragments (value!r / m.group(1)!r / path segment), bypassing the redaction applied to stderr
findings.suggestion: Carry type+length only in select-failure messages (never repr() captured stdout); keep stdout out of every WorldError.
findings.evidence: raise WorldError('select', f'group is not a number: {m.group(1)!r}')

reasoning.observe: _finite_number and the json/regex branches interpolate parsed stdout; run_measure redacts+truncates stderr only.
reasoning.trace: select_number <- run_measure(proc.stdout) -> WorldError.message -> _emit prints to the CLI's stdout, which the skill/wrapup re-read.
reasoning.infer: A secret-shaped stdout fragment near a mistyped selector surfaces verbatim.
reasoning.conclude: ADR-004's 'stdout never stored' is bypassed on three selector-failure paths.

findings.summary: regex selector with an optional (non-participating) capture group raises TypeError, escaping measure_all's WorldError containment
findings.suggestion: Guard m.group(1) is None (and catch TypeError with ValueError) -> WorldError('select', …); add the regression row ('abc','regex:(\\d+)?abc') to the refusal table.

reasoning.observe: _validate_select only checks groups == 1; an optional group passes and can be None at runtime.
reasoning.trace: float(None) -> TypeError, not caught; measure_all catches WorldError only.
reasoning.infer: One bad selector crashes the whole --all batch with a traceback.
reasoning.conclude: Normalize to WorldError so one outcome fails and the rest continue.

findings.summary: A huge JSON integer raises OverflowError inside math.isfinite, escaping measure_all's containment
findings.suggestion: Only apply isfinite to floats (an int is finite by construction) or catch OverflowError -> WorldError('select'); add the regression row ('{"a": '+'9'*400+'}','json:a').
findings.evidence: if isinstance(value,bool) or not isinstance(value,(int,float)) or not math.isfinite(value)

reasoning.observe: math.isfinite converts the int to float first; a 400-digit int raises OverflowError before the raise line.
reasoning.trace: json.loads places no bound on int magnitude; measure_all catches WorldError only.
reasoning.infer: One oversized field crashes the --all run.
reasoning.conclude: Same blast-radius class as the TypeError finding; normalize to WorldError.

findings.summary: select_number's json list-index bounds (valid negative, out-of-range) are untested; a weakened bounds check passes the suite
findings.suggestion: Add ('{"a":[1,2]}','json:a.-1') -> 1 to the parse table and json:a.5 / json:a.-5 on a 2-element list to the refusal table.

reasoning.observe: Three sub-paths of the bounds check have no case.
reasoning.trace: Bounds check is new code under the Tier-1 mutation rationale.
reasoning.infer: Deleting the check or using 0 <= idx would pass.
reasoning.conclude: Coverage gap on new Tier-1 code (P2 per the owning tests lens; core argued P1).

findings.summary: measure_all reloads and re-parses intent.yaml once per outcome via measure_outcome
findings.suggestion: Give measure_outcome an internal variant taking the loaded Intent/Outcome.
findings.evidence: measure_all: load_intent then measure_outcome(root, id) which loads again

reasoning.infer: Redundant parse; also N snapshots across one --all run.

findings.summary: Evidence records the declared cwd label, not the path actually resolved (git-absent fallback)
findings.suggestion: Interpolate a degraded marker when resolve_base_root fell back to the checkout.

reasoning.observe: resolve_base_root falls back to cwd.resolve() when every git probe fails.
reasoning.trace: Label != resolved path in that edge.
reasoning.infer: Audit-trail text only; no decision reads it.

findings.summary: _short_sha's nogit fallback is never asserted on by any test
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test on an uncommitted root asserting the evidence contains '@ nogit'.

reasoning.observe: No test greps nogit; committed fixtures always succeed.
reasoning.trace: Property test hits it but asserts nothing on evidence.

findings.summary: 'measure first' step runs measure.cmd via --dry-run without a per-run human gate
findings.suggestion: Gate the dry-run behind an ask, or reword HOW-IT-WORKS to say only recording is gated.
findings.evidence: run `hm world outcome measure --all --dry-run` and show the table

reasoning.observe: --dry-run still executes run_measure; the skill step is unconditional inside 'Proposing objectives'.
reasoning.trace: 'Proposing objectives' runs only when the operator asks for proposals; HOW-IT-WORKS says 'runs only when asked'.
reasoning.infer: A versioned intent.yaml edit could run a command at the next proposal request.
reasoning.conclude: Claimed contradiction between the skill and the docs' safety statement.
